title: Uniforms, Albert Nicholas lessons, and the China trip
summary: His carnival and Anderson's uniforms, giving lessons to Albert Nicholas as a young sailor, and a planned China trip with Chicago players.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Would that be the one in the band with Paula Barber and Albert Nicholas? I showed you, yes.
Yes, we had a copy of that picture already. They used to play together too in Chicago. In Chicago too.

He gave Albert lessons. Remember on St. Philip's Dream? Why I remember so very well that he gave him lessons is because I was quite young. And he was a young sailor and he was very good looking. And I ran inside and put ribbon in my hair. And Karen sat in the front row and my daddy ran me out. That's what makes me remember him so very well. He was a fine looking sailor coming in. That was the first world war.
Yeah. I remember. I knew him in New York around 1940 to 1945, along that period. He was a good looking man too. He was a fine looking man.
He was a fine looking man. The last I heard him in Chicago. Yes, that's the last I heard him in Chicago.

He came to this country about two years ago, a little over a year ago. And I don't think he ever got to New Orleans. He went to California and he was in Chicago. He's been living in France and Belgium for quite a while. Oh, for five to ten years almost. More? Oh, wow. He just made a quick clip over here about a year ago, a little over a year ago I think.

Oh, they were supposed to go to China. I was in China. You were in the town, Papa? That's what I was saying. He went to China. He went to China. But my father was supposed to go too, he got sick. He was planning, it was planning that he would go along too to China. They were in Chicago at that time. Yes. They were supposed to go to China. But he didn't go, he came back here. Most naturally he was sick, he came home. Yes. But that was one of his ambitions though, to get to China. That we see the whole world. He had, we had all kinds of rocks and different souvenirs that he brought from different places that he traveled. Wood, you know. Petrified, for us would. We had all kinds of rocks and different things from different places that he visited. Yes. He would bring something back. And just from the years that got rid of him. I was wondering if you still had his mouthpiece or whatever. Oh no. I had him around here for a long time, got tired of him throwing at the junk. I had no use for him. It's just like his book. He used to write out his own parts, conic parts. And we kept it a while for the title of the old song, you know. And got tired of him throwing out.
